Paste this into Figma AI with the wireframe attached:

:::writing{variant="standard" id="48317"}
Create a new Figma page named “Add Printer Flow” in the current JusPrin v2 file.

Use the attached wireframe as the source of truth for the UX, content hierarchy, states, and interaction flow. Treat it as a structural wireframe, not a visual-style reference. The black canvas, red outlines, handwritten annotations, state numbers, and explanatory notes are documentation and must not appear inside the finished UI.

Match the established JusPrin v2 design language already present in this Figma file. Reuse its existing components, typography, colors, spacing, radii, icons, buttons, fields, modal styling, and printer imagery wherever possible. Do not invent a separate visual system or modify existing pages.

Design a polished desktop modal flow that opens when the user clicks “Add Printer” on the JusPrin home page. Create a separate, clearly named frame for every distinct state shown in the attached wireframe, including:

1. Initial state — “Add a printer”
   - Ask: “What printer do you have?”
   - Provide one prominent natural-language input that accepts informal descriptions such as “bambu a1 mini,” “the ender with the touchscreen,” or “not sure, it’s the small one.”
   - Include an optional photo drop zone for a photo of the printer, its nameplate, or its box.
   - Include a “Found on your network” section with a discovered-printer row, online status, device identifier, and “Use this” action.
   - Include “Set it up myself” as a secondary text action.
   - Include the appropriate Next-button state.

2. Recognized-printer state
   - Echo the user’s original description above the result.
   - Show one strong printer-result card using the matching printer image from the existing profile assets, printer name, model details, and build volume.
   - Explain the defaults JusPrin will assume, including nozzle, build plate, and material.
   - Provide an optional natural-language correction field for details such as a different nozzle or an AMS/Combo configuration.
   - Include “Not this one” and a prominent “Add this printer” action.

3. Network-printer selection state
   - Show the complete state that follows choosing “Use this” for the discovered printer.
   - Preserve the same confirmation and correction principles as the recognized-printer state.
   - Reconstruct the full design even where the attached wireframe is partially cropped.

4. Ambiguous-recognition state
   - Echo the ambiguous user description.
   - Briefly explain why more information is needed.
   - Present the likely printer candidates clearly and ask one simple discriminating question based only on features the user can easily observe.
   - Avoid technical questions the user would not reasonably know.
   - Provide an easy way to revise the description, upload a photo, or switch to manual setup.

The central product principle is: recognize the printer from whatever evidence the user can provide, and know what not to ask. The experience should feel conversational, confident, forgiving, and appropriate for someone who may not know their printer’s exact model or technical specifications.

Arrange the frames from left to right in the order of the flow. Label the frames outside the UI with descriptive names such as “18a — Initial,” “18b — Recognized,” “18c — Network printer selected,” and “18d — Ambiguous.” Keep annotations outside the product frames.

Build everything with editable layers, Auto Layout, reusable components, and sensible component variants. Use real interface copy rather than lorem ipsum. Maintain accessible contrast, clear focus states, generous click targets, and consistent modal dimensions. Add simple prototype connections between the states, beginning with the existing home-page “Add Printer” action.

Create only this new page and its prototype connections. Do not redesign or overwrite the existing JusPrin v2 pages.
:::

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/agent-docs/jusprin/add-printer-flow-handoff.md
+# Add Printer flow implementation handoff
+
+**Status:** Design handoff for implementation on `jusprin-newui`. Prepared from
+the Figma page **Add Printer Flow** at repository commit `9e772ec46c` on
+2026-09-12.
+
+This task replaces the legacy printer-picker entry point with a short,
+evidence-led setup flow. The user can describe a printer, attach a photo, or
+select a printer found on the network; JusPrin identifies the smallest valid
+set of printer settings, asks only when the evidence is ambiguous, and applies
+the result through OrcaSlicer's existing preset machinery.
+
+Read [product-definition.md](product-definition.md) §2.2,
+[architecture.md](architecture.md), [design-system.md](design-system.md)
+"Writing UI code", and [fork-stewardship.md](fork-stewardship.md) before
+editing. The Figma frames are the visual source of truth. This document covers
+the behavior and implementation details that the frames cannot express.
+
+---
+
+## 1. Scope and decisions already made
+
+Build the four light-mode states labelled **18a–18d** in Figma:
+
+- 18a — initial evidence entry
+- 18b — one printer recognized from a description or photo
+- 18c — one network printer selected
+- 18d — ambiguous evidence requiring a choice
+
+These decisions are settled:
+
+- Use the existing JusPrin design system and keep the new UI consistent with
+  the current native shell.
+- Implement this as a native C++/wxWidgets modal owned by JusPrin. Do not put a
+  WebView over the native application for this flow.
+- Do not design or implement a separate **18e “Set it up myself”** screen.
+- Keep the **Set it up myself** link and route it to OrcaSlicer's existing
+  `ConfigWizard::SP_PRINTERS` flow. This preserves a working escape hatch
+  without adding 18e.
+- Dark-mode layout and visual QA are out of scope for this task. New code must
+  still use semantic tokens rather than light-mode literals, so it remains
+  structurally theme-safe.
+- Do not redesign the Home screen as part of this task. Expose one reusable
+  launcher so a Home **Add Printer** control can call the same flow when that
+  surface exists.
+
+The flow must not silently accept an identification it cannot map to a real,
+available Orca printer profile. A recognizable display name is not enough; a
+successful result ends in a validated preset and variant.
+
+---
+
+## 2. Open the design before writing code
+
+Figma file: **JusPrin v2**  
+Page: **Add Printer Flow**
+
+| State | Node ID | Direct link |
+|---|---:|---|
+| Page overview | `636:375` | `https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=636-375` |
+| 18a — Initial | `636:1246` | `https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=636-1246` |
+| 18b — Recognized | `636:1328` | `https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=636-1328` |
+| 18c — Network selected | `636:1345` | `https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=636-1345` |
+| 18d — Ambiguous | `636:1395` | `https://www.figma.com/design/jo9J1sK9ZZ0vxncWnSp0vH/JusPrin-v2?node-id=636-1395` |
+
+Another implementation agent can open these links in the same browser used for
+this repository. Select a frame and use Figma's **zoom to selection** command
+before comparing measurements.
+
+The original wireframe is available on the design machine at
+`/Users/kenneth/Downloads/Orca Printer Setup Wireframes-selection.png`, but the
+generated Figma page above is the implementation reference.
+
+### Design review notes
+
+- Every frame is a 1280 × 800 light-mode application view with the Home screen
+  dimmed behind a centered modal.
+- The printer-image areas in 18b and 18c are intentionally neutral placeholders
+  in the generated result. Use existing profile artwork when it is already
+  shipped with the profile; otherwise a neutral placeholder is acceptable.
+  Do not download or invent printer artwork.
+- The labels outside the frames overlap slightly in the page overview. That is
+  canvas annotation noise, not an in-product layout instruction.
+- Figma's prototype links 18a **Next** to 18b, network **Use this** to 18c,
+  18b/18c **Not this one** back to 18a, an ambiguous choice to 18b, and
+  **Start over** back to 18a. Figma could not connect an existing Home-page
+  control across pages; implement that entry point in code rather than treating
+  the missing prototype edge as intentional.
+
+---
+
+## 3. User-visible behavior
+
+### 18a — Initial evidence entry
+
+Show all three evidence paths in one modal:
+
+1. A natural-language field headed **What printer do you have?** Accept model
+   names and descriptions such as “bambu a1 mini”, “the Ender with the
+   touchscreen”, or “not sure, it's the small one”.
+2. A photo drop target. Clicking it opens a file picker; dragging a supported
+   image onto it stages that image. The copy should make clear that a photo of
+   the printer, its nameplate, or its box is useful.
+3. A **Found on your network** list. Each row shows the observed printer name,
+   a stable device identifier suitable for distinguishing duplicates, current
+   availability, and **Use this**.
+
+The footer contains **Set it up myself** and **Next**. `Next` is disabled until
+there is usable text or a valid staged photo. Selecting a network row may go
+directly to 18c without requiring `Next`.
+
+Do not require all three evidence sources. Combine the sources that are present
+and omit questions whose answers are already known.
+
+### Recognition progress
+
+The design does not contain a loading frame, but the implementation needs a
+normal, non-blocking progress state:
+
+- Keep the dialog responsive and show recognition in progress in the primary
+  action area.
+- Disable duplicate submissions while one request is active.
+- Closing the dialog or starting over cancels the request.
+- Tag each request with a monotonically increasing generation/request ID and
+  ignore callbacks from older generations.
+- Never change presets while recognition is still running.
+
+### 18b — One printer recognized
+
+Echo the evidence that led to the result, then show one candidate card with:
+
+- canonical display name;
+- build volume read from the matched profile;
+- printer artwork or neutral placeholder;
+- the assumed nozzle, plate, and material;
+- an optional correction field for facts such as “I put a 0.6 nozzle on it”
+  or “it's the Combo with the AMS”.
+
+The footer actions are **Not this one** and **Add this printer**.
+
+`Add this printer` is only enabled when the candidate maps to an installable
+printer model and a real variant. If correction text changes a resolved fact,
+re-resolve and revalidate it before enabling the action. Never display a
+correction as accepted and then discard it.
+
+### 18c — Network printer selected
+
+Use the same confirmation structure as 18b, but identify that the evidence came
+from the network and show the observed connection, for example **Connected ·
+LAN**. A network device match still requires a validated printer model and
+variant; a device name alone is not authority to choose a preset.
+
+Retain the stable device ID in the model even if the visible copy uses the
+friendly name. Two devices with the same nickname must remain distinguishable.
+
+### 18d — Ambiguous evidence
+
+Explain why one answer is not safe, then show the smallest useful candidate
+set. The Figma example distinguishes **Ender 3 V2** from **Ender 3 V2 Neo**.
+Each candidate has a concise distinguishing fact and a **This one** action.
+
+Choosing a candidate moves to 18b with that canonical candidate selected.
+**Upload a photo** returns focus to photo evidence; **Start over** clears all
+evidence and returns to 18a.
+
+Do not show an unbounded printer catalogue here. If more than a small number of
+candidates survive, ask one discriminating question or direct the user to the
+manual wizard.
+
+### Completion
+
+Apply a setup only after the user presses **Add this printer**. On success:
+
+1. enable/install the matched vendor, model, and nozzle variant if necessary;
+2. select the resulting printer preset through Orca's normal preset path;
+3. apply only corrections/defaults that were explicitly resolved and validated;
+4. refresh the printer chip and other dependent UI through the existing Orca
+   events/configuration path;
+5. close the dialog.
+
+If any step fails, keep the dialog open, show a useful error, and leave the
+previous setup intact. Do not report success merely because recognition
+succeeded.
+
+---
+
+## 4. State and data contracts
+
+Keep the decision logic GUI-free. Names below are descriptive rather than a
+required public API.
+
+```text
+PrinterEvidence
+  description: string
+  photo: optional { bytes, mime, original_name }
+  discovered_device: optional stable device snapshot
+
+PrinterCandidate
+  canonical_model_id: string
+  vendor_id: string
+  display_name: string
+  variant: string
+  preset_name: string
+  build_volume: dimensions read from profile
+  supported_nozzles: list read from profiles
+  default_nozzle / plate / material: resolved values, not prose
+  explanation: short user-facing distinguishing fact
+
+RecognitionResult
+  recognized(candidate, assumptions)
+  ambiguous(candidates, question)
+  no_match(message)
+  failed(error)
+
+ResolvedPrinterSetup
+  candidate identity
+  selected nozzle variant
+  optional plate/material corrections
+  optional network device identity
+```
+
+Rules:
+
+- Treat model output as untrusted suggestions. It may return canonical IDs from
+  the candidate catalogue, never an arbitrary preset name that is applied
+  directly.
+- Build the candidate catalogue from Orca's loaded vendor profiles and printer
+  presets. Match the provider's candidate ID back to that catalogue on the GUI
+  side before allowing confirmation.
+- Read build volume, nozzle variants, default materials, and available artwork
+  from the matched profile. Do not hard-code the Bambu and Creality example
+  values from Figma.
+- A 0.4 mm nozzle is a default only when that model actually exposes a matching
+  variant. Plate and PLA assumptions must likewise come from compatible profile
+  data or an explicit product rule represented in one place.
+- Keep provider confidence as diagnostic input, not as the sole decision rule.
+  A single result below the selected threshold becomes an ambiguous/no-match
+  state rather than an automatic selection.
+- Expected outcomes (`recognized`, `ambiguous`, `no_match`) use normal control
+  flow. Transport failures and malformed responses remain visible failures.
+
+### Recognition service boundary
+
+Add a small, flow-specific `IPrinterRecognitionService`. It should be
+asynchronous/poll-driven like the existing Agent service and have both a
+deterministic implementation for tests and a live implementation.
+
+The repository's existing OpenAI transport already supports image input in
+`Agent/OpenAIResponsesAgent.cpp`; shared low-level transport or image encoding
+may be extracted if doing so is genuinely reusable. Do not send this modal's
+request through the Agent conversation or persist it as a chat message. The
+dialog owns a bounded recognition request, not a conversation turn.
+
+The provider response must use a strict structured schema and may refer only to
+candidate IDs supplied in the request. Include enough local candidate metadata
+for the provider to distinguish models, but do not send unrelated workspace or
+project data.
+
+### Photo handling and privacy
+
+- Accept only explicitly selected or dropped images.
+- Validate MIME/type and size before making a request. Reuse existing attachment
+  limits when appropriate instead of creating a larger second policy.
+- Keep bytes in memory or a task-scoped temporary file and remove them when the
+  request/dialog ends.
+- Do not add setup photos to project persistence or conversation history.
+- Show a recoverable error for an unsupported or unreadable file.
+
+### Network discovery boundary
+
+The existing device layer exposes bound/known machines through
+`DeviceManager::get_my_machine_list()`. `SelectMachine.cpp` is a useful
+upstream reference for filtering and sorting online/connected machines.
+
+Create a fork-owned adapter that snapshots only the fields this dialog needs on
+the GUI thread. Do not retain raw `MachineObject*` pointers in asynchronous
+recognition work. The snapshot should include a stable device ID, friendly
+name, reported printer type/model where present, online/connected state, and
+connection kind.
+
+`Testing/FakeBambuAgent` is not a discovery fake: its README explicitly says
+MQTT, FTPS, and discovery are not implemented. Do not expand that fake for this
+task. Exercise discovery behavior through a deterministic dialog provider and
+test the real `DeviceManager` projection separately where practical.
+
+---
+
+## 5. Repository attachment points
+
+### Existing entry point
+
+`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/PrinterMenu.cpp` currently ends its root menu
+with:
+
+```cpp
+add.label = _L("Add a printer…");
+add.invoke = [] {
+    wxGetApp().run_wizard(ConfigWizard::RR_USER, ConfigWizard::SP_PRINTERS);
+};
+```
+
+Replace this callback with one fork-owned launcher. The launcher should accept
+the owning window and `Plater&`, then construct the new modal and its service
+dependencies. Keep the legacy `run_wizard(...)` call behind the modal's **Set
+it up myself** action.
+
+`StatusRow.cpp` already opens `PrinterMenu`; it should not learn the Add Printer
+state machine. A future Home button must call the same launcher rather than
+duplicating the dialog.
+
+### Applying the selected setup
+
+`Shell/SetupCommands::select_printer_preset(Plater&, preset_name)` is the
+existing fork-owned path for selecting an already available preset. It keeps
+object positions, the printer tab, and the Orca configuration change path in
+sync. Reuse or extend this seam; do not drive a hidden combo box and do not
+write the selected preset directly into config.
+
+Recognition can identify models that are shipped but not currently enabled.
+`select_printer_preset` alone does not establish the whole installation
+contract. Before implementing completion, trace the current Config Wizard path
+that stages `AppConfig::set_variant(...)` and applies/reloads the selected
+vendors and default materials. Add the smallest fork-owned command that invokes
+the necessary public Orca behavior. Do not copy `ConfigWizard::priv::apply_config`
+or partially reproduce it inside the dialog.
+
+If Orca exposes no safe public entry point for enabling one variant, stop at
+that seam and add a small, product-neutral upstream API with the rebase evidence
+required by [fork-stewardship.md](fork-stewardship.md). Do not make a recognized
+but disabled profile appear successful.
+
+### Suggested fork-owned files
+
+Exact names may follow nearby conventions, but keep these responsibilities
+separate:
+
+```text
+src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/PrinterSetupDialog.hpp/.cpp
+    native controls, layout, accessibility, rendering only
+
+src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/PrinterSetupController.hpp/.cpp
+    state transitions, cancellation, stale-result suppression, apply sequence
+
+src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/PrinterCatalog.hpp/.cpp
+    immutable projection of Orca profiles into validated candidates
+
+src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/PrinterDiscovery.hpp/.cpp
+    immutable projection of DeviceManager machines
+
+src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/PrinterRecognition.hpp/.cpp
+    service contract, strict response parsing, deterministic/live services
+```
+
+Register new production sources in
+`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/sources.cmake`. Put GUI-free contract tests in the
+existing `jusprin_tests` target, and wx/Orca integration tests in a separate
+GUI-enabled target under `tests/jusprin/CMakeLists.txt` if they cannot fit
+`shell_theme_tests` cleanly.
+
+---
+
+## 6. Design-system requirements
+
+Use `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json` as the source of truth.
+Native code reads it through `ShellTheme`; stock controls are styled through
+`Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp`.
+
+- Every color, radius, font, and control size comes from a token or reusable
+  shell recipe. Do not copy hex values or measurements from the Figma inspect
+  panel into C++.
+- Spacing literals are allowed only when they are already on the documented
+  spacing scale.
+- If the modal scrim, dialog size, drop target, candidate card, or primary
+  action needs a value that has no token, add the component/semantic token
+  first and extend `tests/brand/test_brand_tokens.cpp`.
+- The current general button recipe is secondary-styled. Add a reusable primary
+  button recipe if one does not exist; do not style **Add this printer** locally.
+- Use `FromDIP`/DIP-aware layout, sizers, and platform-native focus behavior.
+- The modal must remain usable when copy expands under localization. Do not
+  position controls with fixed absolute coordinates.
+- The background scrim must not block the dialog's focus or allow clicks to
+  activate the underlying Home/Prepare surface.
+
+The light-only scope means no separate dark Figma frame or dark visual signoff
+is required. It does not waive semantic token use.
+
+---
+
+## 7. Error and recovery states missing from Figma
+
+Implement these as part of the same state machine. Keep the user's evidence in
+place unless they choose **Start over**.
+
+| Condition | Required behavior |
+|---|---|
+| Recognition service unavailable or not configured | Explain that automatic recognition is unavailable; offer retry and **Set it up myself** |
+| Network/HTTP failure | Show a retryable error; do not clear the evidence |
+| Malformed or unknown candidate ID | Treat as a service error; never fall back to the closest preset silently |
+| No match | Say that the printer could not be identified; ask for a model/nameplate photo or offer manual setup |
+| Unsupported/oversized photo | Reject before upload and explain the allowed input |
+| Matched model has no installable variant | Explain that no compatible profile is available and offer manual setup |
+| Apply/install failure | Keep the old printer setup, show the failure, and allow retry/manual setup |
+| Dialog close or Start over during request | Cancel work and ignore any later callback |
+
+Do not catch unexpected errors merely to log them and continue. Translate an
+error only where this boundary can give the user a more useful recovery action.
+
+---
+
+## 8. Verification plan
+
+### GUI-free tests
+
+Cover at least:
+
+- catalogue construction from model/variant fixtures;
+- exact mapping from allowed candidate ID to preset;
+- rejection of an invented, missing, or hidden/uninstallable candidate;
+- recognized, ambiguous, no-match, malformed, and transport-failure results;
+- nozzle correction selecting the matching variant;
+- correction that cannot be honored remains unresolved rather than being
+  silently ignored;
+- stale callback ignored after retry, Start over, or dialog close;
+- confirm is idempotent and cannot apply twice;
+- two network devices with the same nickname remain distinct by device ID;
+- photo validation and cleanup.
+
+### Native integration tests
+
+Cover at least:
+
+- `Add a printer…` opens the new modal from `PrinterMenu`;
+- **Set it up myself** closes/abandons the new flow and opens the existing
+  printer Config Wizard;
+- confirming an already enabled profile selects it through `SetupCommands`;
+- confirming a shipped but disabled profile makes it available, selects it,
+  and survives an application restart using an isolated data directory;
+- failure during installation does not leave a half-selected preset;
+- network **Use this**, **Not this one**, ambiguous **This one**, and **Start
+  over** follow the state transitions in §3;
+- keyboard-only operation, tab order, default/cancel keys, screen-reader names,
+  long labels, and high-DPI rendering.
+
+### Visual checks
+
+Run the application with a scratch `--datadir`; never drive another JusPrin
+instance. Compare all four light-mode states to their direct Figma frames at
+1280 × 800, then check one narrower and one wider supported window. Capture
+screenshots for review. Check that the background is inert, the modal remains
+centered, content is not clipped, and errors/loading do not resize it
+erratically.
+
+Do not use the Bambu in-process fake as proof of discovery. Its supported
+purpose and isolated-instance setup are documented in
+`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.
+
+### Commands
+
+Use the configured platform build. On macOS:
+
+```sh
+cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --
+ctest --test-dir build/arm64 --output-on-failure
+```
+
+Run the focused targets while iterating, including `jusprin_tests`, the new
+dialog/integration target, `brand_tokens_tests`, and `shell_theme_tests`. Run
+`npm test` in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI` only if shared AgentUI code was
+changed.
+
+Before handoff, also run `git diff --check` and record the exact commands,
+results, screenshots, branch, and commit in the implementation summary.
+
+---
+
+## 9. Acceptance criteria
+
+The feature is complete only when all of these are true:
+
+1. The printer menu's **Add a printer…** opens the new native modal.
+2. 18a accepts description, photo, and network evidence independently.
+3. A single validated match reaches 18b; a selected network device reaches
+   18c; ambiguous evidence reaches 18d.
+4. Only the final confirmation changes application setup.
+5. Confirmation enables the required shipped model/variant when necessary,
+   selects the real preset through Orca's normal path, refreshes dependent UI,
+   and persists across restart.
+6. Corrections shown as accepted are actually applied. Unsupported corrections
+   remain visibly unresolved.
+7. **Not this one**, **Start over**, cancel, retry, and stale responses preserve
+   a valid previous setup.
+8. **Set it up myself** opens the existing Orca printer wizard; there is no new
+   18e screen.
+9. No provider string can select an arbitrary preset without catalogue
+   validation.
+10. The four light-mode states match Figma closely at 1280 × 800 and remain
+    usable at narrower/wider sizes and high DPI.
+11. New styling uses design tokens and reusable recipes; no local color,
+    radius, font, or control-size literals are introduced.
+12. Focused tests and a full platform build/test pass, with visual evidence from
+    an isolated application instance.
+
+---
+
+## 10. Explicitly out of scope
+
+- A custom 18e/manual catalogue screen
+- Dark-mode mockups or dark visual QA for this flow
+- A Home screen redesign
+- A new Bambu network/discovery simulator
+- Printer firmware pairing, Wi-Fi credential entry, or cloud account setup
+- New printer-profile definitions or changes to `.3mf` serialization
+- Replacing Orca's existing preset, compatibility, or device layers
+
+If implementation reveals that a profile cannot be safely enabled through a
+public Orca seam, treat that as an integration blocker to resolve explicitly.
+Do not broaden this task into a copied setup wizard or ship a dialog that only
+changes its own presentation state.
*** End Patch";
